method.coldStart: Process/isolate start through first PDF byte, including module instantiation.
method.warmRender: Steady state after warm-up; median and p95 over the published iteration count. Puppeteer reuses one browser across iterations (setContent + page.pdf each).
method.comparisonSurface: All targets and Puppeteer render byte-identical HTML from the fixed corpus, so every column is the same document.
method.twoRuns: Two environments are published side by side and neither is cherry-picked: a dev machine (clean, quiet, single run) shows the engine on good hardware; CI ubuntu-latest (a shared, noisy runner) is the conservative number and the one that is regenerated on every push. Where a document ran on one but not the other, the gap is shown rather than the row hidden.

documents.description: Point-of-sale receipt — the simple single-page shape.
Quarterly report — prose + one table. Continuity with the legacy ~26ms figure.
Table-heavy statement: repeating <thead>, zebra rows, many page breaks.
Paged-media overhead: @page margin boxes, running header/footer, page counters.
Rendered plain AND as PDF/UA-1 + PDF/A-2b — the delta is the cost of conformance.

sentinelFix.method: A/B: pre-fix WASM rebuilt from HEAD~1 vs the fix, same machine/harness, node target, warm median.
sentinelFix.finding: The published ~26ms figure was measured on a document doing two layout passes; the honest single-pass number is ~21ms.

whereWeLose.method: FORME_PROFILE phase timing (native) + examples/allocprofile.rs (counting allocator), invoice-50p and ledger-500p. `*Before` fields are the pre-fix values; current fields are after the Sept-2026 allocation fixes (same M3 Max, Puppeteer as a stable control moved <2%).
whereWeLose.decomposition: Forme originally trailed Puppeteer ~3.8× on ledger-500p, decomposed as two independent linear factors: ~2× from the page-number second layout pass (ledger crosses the 2→3 digit-width boundary at page 100, so it re-lays-out to widen the page-count field), and ~1.9× from per-node allocation churn. That decomposition was directionally right and quantitatively wrong in the engine's favor: fixing the allocation churn (−74% allocations, −88% bytes allocated; benchmarks/harness/dhatprofile) dropped per-pass layout from ~7.3 to ~1.8 ms/page — a ~4× per-pass gain, not the estimated ~1.9×. It isolates cleanly because parse and serialize (both untouched) didn't move. That alone flipped both large docs — ledger 9997→2284 ms, invoice 534→147 ms — from behind Puppeteer to ahead (ledger 2284 vs 2665 ms, invoice 147 vs 232 ms; same M3 Max, Puppeteer as a stable control moved <2%). The ~2× sentinel factor is NOT eliminated: ledger still runs 2 passes — it is now masked by the throughput win, i.e. forme leads while doing twice Chrome's layout work. Removing that second pass on digit-change docs is the remaining known inefficiency (scoping it to just the running element proved unsound — see the sentinel tracked-fix note) and would roughly halve ledger's layout again.
whereWeLose.memoryShape: The full layout tree is retained until serialize (~2 MB/page), so peak memory is linear in document size and freed at exit — not a leak. The allocation fixes did NOT move peak (ledger wasm ~890 MB before and after): they removed transient churn, not retained state — a throughput/allocator-pressure win, not a memory-ceiling one.

trackedFixes.name: Streaming layout — cap peak so large docs render in a 128MB Workers isolate
trackedFixes.note: Investigated 2026-09 across THREE reframings, each cheaper than the build it prevented; parked with a well-scoped next project. (1) "Streaming serialize" is a misnomer — the ~1GB peak is NOT the serializer, which only borrows &[LayoutPage] and is already ~90% streaming-ready (Pass 1 consumes+compresses everything heavy; Pass 2 touches only scalars + lightweight lists). It is the retained Vec<LayoutPage> (~2MB/page) the CALLER holds. (2) "Streaming layout" (a restartable count-then-emit producer) is SOUND — layout() is a deterministic pure function of (document, sentinel_digit_count) so a discarding count pass and an emitting pass produce identical pagination; byte-identity is achievable (only the lifetime of the heavy element vecs changes, provided font/image/gstate/shading registration still runs globally up-front in page-order); compliance is NOT a blocker (TagBuilder/link_slots/StructParents are lightweight, stay whole-document, veraPDF 9/9 by construction); PageCursor forward-state is already resumable. BUT it does nothing for the acceptance-test doc. (3) THE REAL FINDING: the peak on ledger-500p is not "the layout Vec" in general — it is ONE document-spanning table (8001 rows / 500 pages) whose RETROACTIVE wrapper (layout_table mod.rs:3488-3538, and the same pattern in layout_breakable_view, flex, paragraph) reaches back into every page it covered, after the table closes, to wrap each page in a border/background/tag container. For a doc-spanning table "after it closes" is end-of-document, so all 500 pages stay resident regardless of streaming. THE ANSWER is item 3: convert that retroactive wrap into FORWARD, at-page-finalize emission via an open-container stack on the cursor (each open container records draw_cmd + per-page start-y; on finalize it wraps the finalizing page from start-y; on new_page start-y resets to content_top; on close it wraps the current page). Feasible and byte-identical (each wrapper uses only its own page geometry), but it is 4 container types + linearizing table-overflow ordering — the hardest pagination code, highest output-correctness risk, and roughly as large as the two-pass work it enables. SEQUENCING: items 1-2 (streaming producer + writer restructure) are UNOBSERVABLE on the acceptance test until item 3 lands — do NOT start with them expecting a win. Parked because Workers-isolate 500p rendering has zero requesters (real users render invoices/reports well under the ceiling); revisit item 3 as its own byte-identical project, gated by the full corpus + a new isolate acceptance test, only if a real need appears. Peak floor after a full fix (item 3 done): ~3-5MB for ledger — 1 resident page (~1.8MB) + accumulated compressed content objects (≤1.3MB, the single-file-xref floor); going lower needs incremental xref (linearized PDF), out of scope.

trackedFixes.name: Reduce per-node allocation (arena / SmallVec / drop style clones)
trackedFixes.note: dhat-profiled 2026-09 (benchmarks/harness/dhatprofile + dhat-top.mjs). TWO FIXES LANDED, output byte-identical, all gates green. (A) PositionedGlyph.font_family String→Arc<str> — #1 site by allocation COUNT; every glyph owned its own family string, so each of the millions of glyph clones heap-allocated one. Arc<str> makes clone a refcount bump. (B) Table-cell rollback checkpoint elision — the dhat BACKTRACES (not the profile guess of "measure_node_height trial-layout") showed ~76% of all allocated BYTES came from ONE line: layout_table_row cloned the whole PageCursor (which owns elements: Vec<LayoutElement>, every element on the page) before each cell as page-break rollback, then discarded it unused whenever the cell fit. Guard added: skip the clone when the row fits (row_height <= remaining_height) and its subtree forces no break — byte-identical by construction since an elided checkpoint would never be restored. Combined result: allocations −74% (ledger-500p 182.8M→46.3M, invoice-50p 9.24M→2.45M), bytes allocated −88% (invoice-50p 2476MB→304MB). Peak memory unchanged (churn, not peak). REMAINING (Design 2, parked): the residual at-risk-cell clones near page boundaries — a length-based checkpoint replacing the clone entirely — carry intricate mem::take/cell_pages rollback semantics + ~20-field exhaustive capture; own go/no-go, likely not worth it after (B).

trackedFixes.name: Sentinel re-pass re-measures only the running element
trackedFixes.note: Investigated 2026-09 and set aside: not scopable as written. The sentinel width is consumed during injection (footer/margin-box layout), not the flow pass, and HTML @page margin boxes are Fixed nodes — so a "reuse flow + re-inject" split has no guard signal to read and silently skips the correction (byte-identity caught it). Would need injection-time or model-scan detection.

coldStart.caveat: miniflare runs a workerd subprocess whose routing overhead the real edge does not pay; wall time OVERSTATES production cold start (true edge isolate spin-up ~5ms). Instantiate/render split is accurate. Real production cold start needs a deployment (out of scope).

coldStart.coldServerlessNote: On real serverless, cold Chrome is 3-10s, and on many consumption tiers a browser cannot boot at all.
